newsitem.title: INDIA: INDIAN CASTORSEED SLUMPS ON PROFIT-TAKING.
newsitem.headline: INDIAN CASTORSEED SLUMPS ON PROFIT-TAKING.

text.p: Castorseed September delivery nosedived to 1,168/1,170 rupees per quintal from 1,180 rupees on profit taking, floor sources said on Tuesday.
Absence of fresh overseas demand and improved supplies prompted profit-taking by the bull operators.
Daily average arrivals of castorseed in the Gujarat region remained higher at 11,000/12,000 bags (75 kg each).
"Meanwhile no trading was reported in the castorseed December delivery," one operator said.

Groundnut oil fell by two rupees to 376/377 rupees per 10 kg on improved arrivals of 80/100 tonnes against 40/50 tonnes recorded on Monday. Inflow was mainly from southern India while supplies from Gujarat region remained low in the Bombay market. In Rajkot it was steady at 588/590 rupees per 15 kg.
In Bombay imported palm oil slid by two rupees to 260 rupees per 10 kg as local importers booked profits on expectation of fresh arrivals at the port shortly.
